title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein
snippet:
Dragon Slayer Ornstein -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : Ornstein seems to hold a consistent presence across all three *Dark Souls* games in some form or another:
**He appears as a boss alongside Smough in *Dark Souls*.
**The Old Dragonslayer is a boss in *Dark Souls II* that dons a black version of Ornstein's armor and utilizes dark magic. Whether the Dragonslayer is Ornstein himself or an impostor is unknown.
**The Dragonslayer Armour is noticeably inspired by Ornstein; aside from visual similarities between the two (including both possessing a red plume), the Dragonslayer Armour utilizes lightning in some of its attacks. It is also revealed in the Dragonslayer Set description that Ornstein left Anor Londo in search of the Nameless King.
Ornstein's name, alongside the Leo Ring, are homages to Russian-American composer, Leo Ornstein, an experimental composer of the early 20th century.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough
snippet:
In *Dark Souls III*, Executioner Smough is referenced as the last knight in defense of the last cathedral of Anor Londo.. This was after Ornstein abandoned his duty to search for The Nameless King, leaving Ornstein alone. This represents the main explicit retcon of the Dark Souls series as in *Dark Souls* not only the presence but also the death of Ornstein were canon, as his soul and his ring that gave him the title of knight could be obtained.
In co-op it is possible for multiple players to be caught by Giant Ornstein's Lightning Impale attack at the same time. However, neither player will take any damage from the attack when this happens.
Smough can be heard laughing during the fight. His laugh is noticeably similar to the laugh of the Fat Official from *Demon's Souls*.
Ornstein is named after the composer and pianist Leo Ornstein. This explains the lion-themed motif of Ornstein's helmet.

title: Executioner Smough
snippet:
Executioner Smough -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Smough was the royal executioner of Anor Londo in service of the Gods, wielding a massive hammer and wearing grotesque armor. He derived great pleasure from his work, to the point of being depicted as an "eerily gleeful" executioner. It is stated that he used to ground the bones of his victims beneath his hammer and consume them with his food; this ghastly habit might be what tempered his hammer's ability to absorb the lifeforce of adversaries. Smough also desired to be a part of the Four Knights of Gwyn, but his monstrous behaviour instead led to him being shunned and feared by the honourable knights.

At some point after Gwyn linked the First Flame and Gwyn's firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, nearly all of the deities abandoned Anor Londo and moved to an unknown location. Smough remained in the forsaken city alongside Dragon Slayer Ornstein to guard the cathedral where Gwynevere resided.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough
snippet:
Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : Ornstein and Smough represent the last ritual challenge for the potential Chosen Undead. In fact, the Undead who tried to follow in Gwyn's footsteps to sacrifice themselves to the First Flame would have to be tested even before obtaining the Lordvessel and seeking powerful souls. Ringing the Bells of Awakening represents only the first of these challenges, and success means gaining access to Sen's Fortress to be tested further. The Undead who manage to overcome the tests and dangers of the fortress and defeat the Iron Golem would manage to access Anor Londo. Once they managed to enter the cathedral of the city of the gods to try to obtain the Lordvessel they would still be challenged by Ornstein and Smough guarding it, to ensure that only the strongest of the strongest Undead could have an audience with "Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight".

title: Executioner Smough
snippet:
Executioner Smough -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : After centuries of waiting for the Chosen Undead without success, Ornstein grew tired of his duty and left the cathedral in search of the Nameless King. Consequently, the last remaining guard was Smough, who continued to hold his post and protect "Gwynevere". As a reward for his loyalty, Gwyndolin finally granted him the title of "knight," even if he was the last one left in Anor Londo after all others had abandoned it. As the cathedral's sole guardian, Smough met his end when a worthy Undead reached Anor Londo and defeated him, gaining an audience with "Gwynevere" and the Lordvessel with which to begin their search for powerful souls.

Smough's ritual hammer was preserved as a relic by Gwyndolin and protected in his manor when Irithyll of the Boreal Valley rose from the ruins of Anor Londo.

snippet: However, the Blue Sentinels continued to exist past the falls of both Heide and Drangleic, with the dutiful Targray still standing watch at the Cathedral of Blue, and providing those worthy with Cracked Blue Eye Orbs and a lightning miracle similar to those of the Gods of Anor Londo, while in the town of Majula, which acts as an entry point and home base to new Undead in Drangleic, a crestfallen warrior, Saulden, introduced newcomers to the Way of Blue, ensuring that they received the Sentinels' assistance should they wish for it. title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein
snippet: Together, these two powerful warriors would become the last ritual challenge before a Chosen Undead could be rewarded with the Lordvessel. Only after a lethal and lengthy trial, which involved ringing the Bells of Awakening and surviving Sen's Fortress, could the Chosen Undead be granted entry into the city of the gods. Here, guarding the chambers of Gwynevere, Ornstein waited alongside Smough, and oversaw those seeking an audience with the Princess of Sunlight. However, after centuries of waiting for the Chosen Undead without success, Ornstein grew tired of his duty, and left the cathedral under his companion's watch, to search for the Nameless King, while leaving behind the ring that symbolized his membership in the Four Knights of Gwyn. Ornstein's ring was preserved as a relic by Dark Sun Gwyndolin and protected in his manor when Irithyll of the Boreal Valley rose from the ruins of Anor Londo.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough
snippet:

 first_phase_ornstein_and_smough : The player must fight both at the same time. When one is killed, the other absorbs some of his power, receiving an HP, damage, and resistance boost, and healing back to 100%. He will also take on a physical characteristic of his fallen comrade: Ornstein grows in size while Smough is imbued with lightning.

Having a summoned phantom can make the fight significantly easier, as it allows the bosses to be fought separately. Note, however, that there's no advantage in damaging both bosses during the first phase (as mentioned above, the surviving boss' HP goes back to 100% when the second phase begins). The role of the second player is simply to keep one of the bosses busy while the other is killed.

 lore : Ornstein is one of the knights at the service of Lord of Sunlight, and one of those who took part in his Lord's war against the Dragons. He wore a golden armor made to resemble a lion, and wielded a great cross spear which, combined with its wielder's great strength, could bury itself deep within a dragon's hide, piercing their stone scales; and send mere human flying. snippet: After the death of the Blacksmith Deity who was responsible for forging the weapons and armor of the gods, his task was assigned to a giant who thus became the new blacksmith of the gods, and came to work and reside inside the cathedral of Anor Londo. title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein
snippet:
During the war against the dragons Ornstein fought valiantly together with Gwyn's firstborn son, obtaining the title of "Dragon Slayer Knight" and becoming one of Gwyn's most trusted knights. Once his Lord won the war, exterminating the ancient dragons and conquering the world, Ornstein, along with Artorias, Ciaran and Gough, became part of the Four Knights of Gwyn as their captain. As a symbol of his association with the order he gained a magical ring with the lion symbol, which strengthened counter attacks with thrust weapons, making his fighting style with his cross spear more effective.

Ornstein would also become the first knight of Gwyn's firstborn, having accompanied him during the war against dragons. The story of the battles of Ornstein, Gwyn's unnamed firstborn son, and the dragonslayers in their service, were manifested as miracles of war; these were taught to the Warriors of Sunlight, a group of knights that had joined in covenant with the god of war and heir of Gwyn.

The Dragonslayer Armour will occasionally spurt blood when hit, and grunt when attacking. It is unknown whether this implies that the owner's body was still inside the armor when it was possessed, or if it's simply a developer oversight.
The Dragonslayer Armor bears a strong resemblance to the Berserker Armor from the *Berserk* anime/manga.

During the founding of the kingdom, the soldiers of Lothric had found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns and had to rise to the challenge, ascending common knighthood. And so these armors of Lothric's first knights were crafted: heavy masses of iron capable of withstanding dragon fire, similar in design to the ancient armor of the dragonslayers of Anor Londo, with their shields capable of absorbing the lightning breath of wyverns.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: Following her exodus, the only deity left to protect Anor Londo was her younger brother Dark Sun Gwyndolin. However, he was more than aware of his fragile, repulsive appearance and was psychologically unfit to become the next ruler, still playing the feminine role imposed on him by his father Gwyn. For this reason, Gwyndolin created an illusion of Gwynevere to help him maintain some semblance of divinity and control over the ancient capital. Over time this illusion of the goddess would become a key component in the system that sought a worthy champion to link the First Flame, serving to guide and manipulate potential Chosen Undead, with Kingseeker Frampt imploring them to journey to Anor Londo and seek an audience with the Princess. Much more shady was the role of Gwyndolin, the only true God that remained in Anor Londo. He created an illusion of Gwynevere, Lord Gwyn's daughter, to hide the fact that she had left Anor Londo and married the Flame God, Flann. snippet:

 dark_souls : It's unclear when these distant relatives of dragons made their firs appearance, but they were already around by the time of Lordran, employed by the Gods as workers and guardians of Sen's Fortress, the only way to reach Anor Londo from the outside world. The serpentine wardens would kill anyone who would tempt fate and challenge the fortress's many traps, the mages especially favoring torture and blood-letting in their methods.

They wouldn't kill all of them, however. Those who had grown weary and fatigued would be ambushed and captured, locked away in the many cages dangling from the fortress, to be moved somewhere else, provided the Man Serpents didn't forget about the captive and leave them to rot in their cage. Not many knew what would become of the prisoners that had been brought elsewhere, but it's very likely that their destination was the Duke's Archives, where the Paledrake Seath resided.

title: Lord Gwyn's Firstborn
snippet:
Long ago, the Nameless King was a god of war and heir to lightning. The firstborn was a god of war, and inherited sunlight, which manifests as lightning.
The Nameless King wielded the Dragonslayer Swordspear, a weapon from the Age of Gods. The firstborn similarly wielded a great spear.
The firstborn eventually committed a grave error in the eyes of Anor Londo, which led to the rescinding of his deific status and his removal from the annals of history, his name forgotten. The Nameless King sacrificed everything to ally with the ancient dragons, whom he once fought.
The Nameless King wore a crown and bracelets that greatly resemble those once worn by Gwyn, the First Lord.
Dragon Slayer Ornstein, once the faithful first knight of the Sun's firstborn, left Anor Londo in the dragonless age in search of the Nameless King. His weapon, a cross spear, is extremely similar to that wielded by the Nameless King.

title: Londor
snippet: roots : The origins of Londor can be traced back to when the Primordial Serpent Kaathe welcomed three human sisters into his service as his maidens: Elfriede, the eldest; Yuria, the middle child; and Liliane, the youngest. Kaathe's past attempts to uncover a Dark Lord, to prevent the linking of the First Flame, and to finally bring about the Age of Dark had largely failed; the order of the old gods remained dominant and the Age of Fire persevered, albeit increasingly faintly. His failures notwithstanding, the Primordial Serpent was steadfast in his pursuit, and eventually enlisted the sisters as his capable hands. And so Kaathe taught the three sisters, already highly skilled fencers, the art of the Dark Hand, used for absorbing the humanity of its victims. In turn, they used their battle prowess to establish **the Sable Church**, an organization that claimed to offer salvation to Hollows. They settled in the land that would become known as Londor, "the Hollow Realm".

title: Homing Soulmass
snippet:
The main weakness of Soulmasses is that the timing at which they fire cannot be controlled. This makes it somewhat ineffective against melee enemies using shields, as it tends to fire while they are guarding, doing significantly reduced damage, whereas other projectile sorceries can be timed to hit when the enemy goes into an animation in which their guard is down. Another weakness of Soulmassess is that when fighting larger opponents, such as the Bounding Demon of Izalith, the spell will activate prematurely and expire before reaching the target's actual hitbox unless the player or the target run towards each other.

Against ranged attack enemies, and many bosses, who don't use shields, the spell is extremely effective, as the player can focus on blocking or dodging while it fires, and prepare new Soulmasses while in cover or between attacks. This is particularly useful in the fight against Dragonslayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough, for example.

The rank of Dragonrider was reserved for honorable warriors who helped found Drangleic. Together with the King, they crushed the land's former inhabitants and erected a magnificent kingdom upon their graves.

Those wishing to join the ranks of the Dragonriders were forced to undergo intense and dangerous training. Only those who passed the training were allowed in the order, those who failed would be ripped apart by the very mounts they tried to command.

title: Man Serpent (Lore)
snippet: In truth, the Man Serpents were employed as jailers by the dragon, to guard the many prisoners he'd later use for experimentation. The Archive Tower where they toiled was once a repository of impressive knowledge before being turned into a prison. It's clear that Seath did not employ these slithering guards for their intellect, as they were not aware of the value of the things they were guarding. They were also quite careless with the prison's keys, scattering many of them around the Archives with little care.

title: Fenito
snippet:
At some point, the Fenito came into contact with the Leydia Witches and Pyromancers, who worshipped Galib, God of Disease. They allowed them to reside within the Undead Crypt, likely wishing to work together and ensure a peaceful rest to the dead. However, the Leydia apostles soon grew conceited, misusing and disrespecting death. For that transgression they were branded as blasphemous traitors and destroyed. They would never find rest, however, being denied peaceful deaths and put to work as guardians for all time to come.

Despite having been created to guard the Undead Crypt, and upholding this duty with the utmost care throughout countless generations, some Grave Wardens have been seen prowling the noxious halls of Earthen Peak, domain of the Baneful Queen Mytha. The reason why they ventured so far from their post is unkown, and can only be speculated upon.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Despite his harsh upbringing, and having accepted his identity in the eyes of the other deities as fragile and repulsive, Gwyndolin would grow up with a deep admiration for his father and an aspiration to become like him, wearing a crown with the design of the sun that was imbued with his dark moon magic. He accepted his place and role to the point of supporting his father's will even after his death, and he took part in the workings of his kingdom. title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Both the Orb and Arrow Spread attacks are avoidable by hiding behind one of the pillars on either side of the corridor. The Sphere Shot, on the other hand, will go through walls, inflicting full damage if not blocked or avoided. The Orb Spread and Sphere Shot are Magic-based, though, so a shield that can block 100% physical damage and has good Magic resistance, like the Crest Shield, is recommended for this fight.

While devastating, both the Sphere Shot and Arrow Spread attacks have no tracking whatsoever and are easily avoided simply by running diagonally. If a player does not want to risk it too much, a good strategy to catch up to him is by moving from pillar to pillar until they are about two pillars away from Gwyndolin and then wait until he shoots his Arrow Spread. This attack can consist of two-to-four arrow barrages. Wait until he finishes the second one and go for him, if he shoots any subsequent arrows, dodge them by running diagonally.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein
snippet:
Ornstein's name, alongside the Leo Ring, are homages to Russian-American composer, Leo Ornstein, an experimental composer of the early 20th century.
Ornstein's data names in *Dark Souls* are and , addressing his first and second boss fight phases, respectively. It is possibly a reference to the character Griffith, from the anime/manga series *Berserk,* which was a source of inspiration throughout the development of the series.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough
snippet: Ranged builds using the pillars to control the movement of the bosses should note that not all pillars are the same height; some will block projectiles while others will not.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough
snippet:
When fighting alone, one of the safest strategies is to kite the bosses around the outside of the room, keeping both in view and using the pillars to block their charging attacks while whittling them down with hit-and-run tactics. As Ornstein is the faster of the pair, he will usually be able to catch up to the player quickly. The player can then choose to focus down Ornstein while Smough attempts to navigate around the pillars, or double back to Smough after getting Ornstein away from him and using the short window of separation to attack him before Ornstein returns.

Ornstein's moveset consists largely of dashing and thrusting attacks, meaning that dodging to his sides is more effective than attempting to roll away. He is faster and more nimble though, so he can also be harder to hit. As well, he can issue Lightning blasts from his spear at range, making him a serious threat at any distance.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough
snippet:
Smough is the tougher of the two, his hammer is capable of dealing tremendous damage should it connect. Because the hitbox is centered on the head of the hammer, it is best to dodge towards or away from him, as getting within the arc of his hammer's horizontal swings can cause them to miss entirely. Beware, as he also has a dangerous charge attack that he can use if the player is not within striking distance of his hammer.

Killing Ornstein first is generally regarded as making the encounter easier to win, since Smough has more weaknesses and is slower than his partner in the second phase. However, killing Smough first will yield the Leo Ring, which is a useful ring for certain builds.

For melee builds, using a weapon with good reach (such as a spear, halberd or a sword with a fast thrusting attack) will make it significantly easier to hit the bosses when they are near a pillar. Note that both bosses can hit through the pillars with some of their attacks.

This is because his immense armor was preserved for centuries despite its model no longer being in use and placed in the center of a small bridge as a monument. title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: In the last days of Lothric, as the First Flame was almost faded, flocks of Pilgrim Butterflies would manifest in the Lothric skies. These gigantic humanoid insects with immense, branch-like wings would infest the skies of the dying kingdom, migrating towards the tip of Lothric Castle. Here they would take control of the statue of a Dragonslayer Armour through dark magic, using it as a puppet to eliminate anyone who attempted to proceed to the top of the castle.

snippet: The old knights of Lothric also turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, who in turn gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

Dragonslayer Armour -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : The Dragonslayer Armour uses attacks that are characterized by gulf swings and occasional overhead attacks. It deals large amounts of damage to any character regardless of their resistances. The best tactic for dealing with this boss is to constantly roll away from its attacks and land one of your own. It also deals a huge amount of stamina damage if you try blocking.

It is essential when fighting this boss to remain under 70% Equip Load so that you can roll at a fast pace. Since the fight will be characterized by dodging, it would be advisable to not be overencumbered and have a slow pace roll.

The boss uses its greataxe for overhead chops and wide gulf swings, but it will use its shield with startling speed to break your defense. In the second stage of the fight, it will use shield combos or use its shield before its greataxe.
